parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which equation represents the first ionisation energy of chlorine?
A Cl(g) → Cl⁺(g) + e⁻
B ½Cl₂(g) → Cl⁺(g) + e⁻
C Cl(g) + e⁻ → Cl⁻(g)
D Cl⁻(g) → Cl(g) + e⁻
parts.answer: A Cl(g) → Cl⁺(g) + e⁻
parts.working: First ionisation energy is for one mole of gaseous atoms each losing one electron to form one mole of gaseous 1+ ions. B starts from the molecule (it includes atomisation); C is electron affinity; D removes an electron from an anion.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Define the term first ionisation energy.
parts.answer: The energy needed to remove one electron from each atom in one mole of gaseous atoms to form one mole of gaseous 1+ ions.
parts.working:
M1 energy to remove one electron from each atom in 1 mole of atoms
M2 atoms and ions are gaseous (1+ ions formed)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write an equation, with state symbols, for the second ionisation energy of magnesium.
parts.answer: Mg⁺(g) → Mg²⁺(g) + e⁻
parts.working: B1 correct species and state symbols

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the second ionisation energy of magnesium is greater than its first ionisation energy.
parts.answer: The electron is removed from a positive ion; there is the same nuclear charge but fewer electrons, so less repulsion and the remaining electrons are held more tightly / the outer electron is closer to the nucleus.
parts.working:
M1 electron removed from a positive ion / greater attraction (effective nuclear charge per electron greater)
M2 same number of protons but fewer electrons so less shielding/repulsion; radius of ion smaller

stem:
The first ionisation energies of the Period 3 elements, in kJ/mol, are:
Na 496, Mg 738, Al 578, Si 787, P 1012, S 1000, Cl 1251, Ar 1521.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why there is a general increase in first ionisation energy from sodium to argon.
parts.answer: Nuclear charge increases across the period while shielding stays roughly the same (electrons added to the same shell), so the outer electron is held more strongly / atomic radius decreases.
parts.working:
M1 nuclear charge (number of protons) increases
M2 similar shielding / same shell, so greater attraction for outer electrons

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the first ionisation energy of aluminium is lower than that of magnesium.
parts.answer: In Al the electron is removed from a 3p orbital, which is higher in energy (further from the nucleus) and is shielded by the 3s electrons, so less energy is needed.
parts.working:
M1 Al outer electron in 3p (Mg in 3s)
M2 3p is higher in energy / further from nucleus / extra shielding by 3s²

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the first ionisation energy of sulfur is lower than that of phosphorus.
parts.answer: In S the electron is removed from a 3p orbital containing a pair of electrons; repulsion between the paired electrons makes it easier to remove. P has three unpaired 3p electrons.
parts.working:
M1 S has a paired electron in one 3p orbital (3p⁴); P is 3p³ with no pairs
M2 spin-pair repulsion makes the paired electron easier to remove

author: HomiLabs

stem:
The first six successive ionisation energies of element Y, in kJ/mol, are:
578, 1817, 2745, 11 577, 14 842, 18 379.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Deduce the group of the Periodic Table that element Y belongs to. Explain your answer.
parts.answer: Group 13; the large jump is between the 3rd and 4th ionisation energies, so Y has 3 outer-shell electrons.
parts.working:
M1 big jump between IE3 (2745) and IE4 (11 577)
M2 three electrons in outer shell, so Group 13

parts.label: b
parts.text: Y is in Period 3. Identify Y and write the electronic configuration of the ion Y³⁺.
parts.answer: Aluminium; Al³⁺ is 1s² 2s² 2p⁶

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why each successive ionisation energy of Y is larger than the one before.
parts.answer: Each electron is removed from an increasingly positive ion, so there is less repulsion and greater attraction to the nucleus.
parts.working: B1 removing electron from more positive ion / same nuclear charge holding fewer electrons

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text:
The first six successive ionisation energies of an element, in kJ/mol, are:
787, 1577, 3232, 4356, 16 091, 19 805
In which group of the Periodic Table is the element?
A Group 2
B Group 13
C Group 14
D Group 15
parts.answer: C Group 14
parts.working: The large jump comes between the 4th (4356) and 5th (16 091) ionisation energies, so the element has 4 outer electrons: Group 14 (silicon). Group 15 would show the jump after the 5th value.

stem: Ionisation energies in kJ/mol: magnesium 1st 738, 2nd 1451; calcium 1st 590, 2nd 1145.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the total energy needed to convert one mole of gaseous atoms into one mole of gaseous 2+ ions for (i) magnesium and (ii) calcium.
parts.answer: (i) 2189 kJ/mol (ii) 1735 kJ/mol

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain the difference between your two answers.
parts.answer: Calcium's outer electrons are in the 4th shell, further from the nucleus and shielded by more inner shells. Although Ca has more protons, the extra distance and shielding outweigh this, so attraction is weaker and less energy is needed.
parts.working:
M1 Ca outer electrons in a higher shell / larger atomic radius
M2 more shielding by inner electrons
M3 increase in nuclear charge is outweighed, so weaker attraction

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest how this difference relates to the reactions of magnesium and calcium with cold water.
parts.answer: Calcium reacts much more readily with cold water than magnesium because it loses its two outer electrons more easily.
parts.working: B1 Ca more reactive (reacts readily with cold water; Mg very slowly) because ions form more easily

author: HomiLabs

stem: A student plots log₁₀(ionisation energy) against the number of the electron removed for all 19 electrons of a potassium atom.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Between which successive ionisation energies would you expect the three large jumps to occur? Explain.
parts.answer: Between the 1st and 2nd, between the 9th and 10th, and between the 17th and 18th, because potassium is 2,8,8,1: each jump marks the start of removing electrons from a shell closer to the nucleus.
parts.working:
B1 1st→2nd
B1 9th→10th and 17th→18th
B1 each jump = removing from a new inner shell, closer to nucleus / less shielded

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why, between the jumps, the ionisation energies rise steadily rather than staying constant.
parts.answer: Each electron removed leaves an ion with more positive charge relative to the remaining electrons, so less repulsion and the ion shrinks; each next electron is attracted more strongly.
parts.working:
M1 increasing positive charge on ion / fewer electrons for same nuclear charge
M2 less repulsion / smaller radius so stronger attraction

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the sub-shell from which the 2nd electron is removed.
parts.answer: 3p

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which Period 2 element has a first ionisation energy greater than that of both of the elements next to it in the period?
A boron
B carbon
C nitrogen
D oxygen
parts.answer: C nitrogen
parts.working: N (1402 kJ/mol) is above C (1086) and O (1314): N has a half-filled 2p sub-shell with no paired electrons, while O has one paired 2p electron that is easier to remove. Boron is below beryllium; carbon is below nitrogen.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the electronic configurations of nitrogen and oxygen atoms using orbital notation (e.g. 1s² …).
parts.answer: N 1s² 2s² 2p³; O 1s² 2s² 2p⁴

parts.label: b
parts.text: The first ionisation energy of nitrogen is 1402 kJ/mol and that of oxygen is 1314 kJ/mol. Explain why oxygen's value is lower although it has more protons.
parts.answer: Oxygen's electron is removed from a 2p orbital that holds two electrons; the repulsion between the paired electrons makes it easier to remove. In nitrogen each 2p orbital holds one electron.
parts.working:
M1 O has a pair of electrons in one 2p orbital
M2 spin-pair repulsion outweighs the extra nuclear charge

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the energy, in kJ, needed to convert 0.500 g of gaseous nitrogen atoms into N⁺ ions. Give your answer to 3 significant figures. [Ar: N, 14.0]

parts.label: a
parts.text: State three factors that affect the size of the first ionisation energy of an atom.
parts.answer: Nuclear charge; distance of the outer electron from the nucleus (atomic radius); shielding by inner electrons. (Spin-pair repulsion also accepted.)
parts.working: B1 each for any three of: nuclear charge; atomic radius/distance; shielding; spin-pair repulsion / sub-shell

parts.label: b
parts.text: State whether sodium or potassium has the lower first ionisation energy and explain your answer.
parts.answer: Potassium; its outer electron is in the 4th shell, further from the nucleus with more shielding, so it is less strongly attracted.
parts.working:
B1 potassium
B1 outer electron further from nucleus / more shielding (outweighs larger nuclear charge)

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which species has more electrons than protons and more neutrons than protons?
A ³⁹K⁺
B ¹⁶O²⁻
C ³⁷Cl⁻
D ²⁷Al³⁺
parts.answer: C ³⁷Cl⁻
parts.working: ³⁷Cl⁻: 17 protons, 20 neutrons, 18 electrons. ¹⁶O²⁻ has more electrons but equal protons and neutrons (8 and 8); ³⁹K⁺ and ²⁷Al³⁺ have fewer electrons than protons.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons in each of: ⁵⁶Fe³⁺, ³²S²⁻ and ⁶⁵Cu⁺.
parts.answer:
⁵⁶Fe³⁺: 26 p, 30 n, 23 e
³²S²⁻: 16 p, 16 n, 18 e
⁶⁵Cu⁺: 29 p, 36 n, 28 e
parts.working: B1 for each correct species (all three numbers right)

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the relative mass and relative charge of a neutron and of an electron.
parts.answer: Neutron: mass 1, charge 0. Electron: mass 1/1836 (about 0.0005), charge −1.
parts.working:
B1 neutron 1 and 0
B1 electron 1/1836 and −1

stem: A beam of particles is passed through an electric field between two parallel charged plates in a vacuum.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe what happens to beams of protons, neutrons and electrons as they pass between the plates.
parts.answer: Protons are deflected towards the negative plate; electrons are deflected towards the positive plate, through a much larger angle; neutrons pass straight through undeflected.
parts.working:
B1 protons towards negative plate
B1 electrons towards positive plate, larger angle
B1 neutrons not deflected

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why electrons are deflected through a much larger angle than protons.
parts.answer: Same size of charge but an electron's mass is about 1/1836 of a proton's, so its charge/mass ratio is much bigger.
parts.working: B1 deflection depends on charge/mass; electron much lighter

parts.label: c
parts.text: A beam of ¹H⁺ ions is deflected through 12.0°. Assuming the angle is proportional to charge/mass, calculate the angle of deflection for a beam of ⁴He²⁺ ions under the same conditions.
parts.working:
M1 charge/mass for ⁴He²⁺ = 2/4 = 0.5 of that of ¹H⁺
A1 12.0 × 0.5 = 6.0°

author: HomiLabs

stem: A sample of boron used in borosilicate glass at a factory in Lahore contains 19.9% ¹⁰B (isotopic mass 10.013) and 80.1% ¹¹B (isotopic mass 11.009) by number of atoms.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Define the term isotopes.
parts.answer: Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why ¹⁰B and ¹¹B have the same chemical properties.
parts.answer: They have the same number of electrons / the same electronic configuration (chemistry depends on electrons).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the relative atomic mass of boron in this sample. Give your answer to 4 significant figures.

author: HomiLabs

stem: Gallium, used in LEDs, has two stable isotopes, ⁶⁹Ga and ⁷¹Ga. Its relative atomic mass is 69.72.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the percentage abundance of ⁶⁹Ga. Assume the isotopic masses are 69.0 and 71.0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons in the ion ⁷¹Ga³⁺.
parts.answer: 31 protons, 40 neutrons, 28 electrons

parts.label: c
parts.text: Gallium's first ionisation energy is lower than that of zinc, the element before it. Suggest why, in terms of electronic configuration.
parts.answer: Ga's outer electron is a single 4p electron, higher in energy and shielded by the full 4s² (and 3d¹⁰); Zn loses an electron from a full 4s sub-shell.
parts.working:
M1 Ga electron removed from 4p (Zn from 4s)
M2 4p higher energy / further / shielded by 4s

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: An ion X²⁻ has 18 electrons and a nucleon number of 34. Identify X and give the number of neutrons in the ion.
parts.answer: Sulfur (³⁴S²⁻); 18 neutrons

parts.label: b
parts.text: An ion Z³⁺ has the same electronic configuration as a neon atom and contains 14 neutrons. Write the full symbol of the ion, showing nucleon number and proton number.
parts.answer: ²⁷₁₃Al³⁺
parts.working:
M1 13 protons (10 + 3) so aluminium
A1 nucleon number 27

parts.label: a
parts.text: Arrange the beams ¹H⁺, ³He²⁺, ⁴He²⁺ and ⁷Li⁺ in order of increasing angle of deflection in an electric field. Show your reasoning.
parts.answer: ⁷Li⁺ < ⁴He²⁺ < ³He²⁺ < ¹H⁺

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the direction in which all four beams are deflected and why.
parts.answer: Towards the negative plate, because they are all positively charged.

stem: Natural chlorine contains 75% ³⁵Cl and 25% ³⁷Cl by number of atoms. A sample of chlorine gas, Cl₂, is analysed in a mass spectrometer.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the m/z values of the three peaks caused by Cl₂⁺ ions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the ratio of the heights of these three peaks. Show your working.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the total number of neutrons in one ³⁷Cl–³⁷Cl molecule.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the full electronic configuration of a silicon atom.
parts.answer: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p²

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the full electronic configuration of an iron atom and of an Fe²⁺ ion.
parts.answer: Fe: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁶ 4s²; Fe²⁺: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁶
parts.working:
B1 Fe
B1 Fe²⁺ (4s electrons lost)

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the number of unpaired electrons in an Fe²⁺ ion.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
What is the electronic configuration of a Cr³⁺ ion?
A [Ar] 3d³
B [Ar] 3d¹ 4s²
C [Ar] 3d² 4s¹
D [Ar] 3d⁴ 4s¹
parts.answer: A [Ar] 3d³
parts.working: Cr is [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹. On forming ions the 4s electron is lost first, then two 3d electrons: [Ar] 3d³. Option B wrongly removes 3d electrons before 4s.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the electronic configurations of chromium and copper atoms in the form [Ar] ….
parts.answer: Cr [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹; Cu [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the electronic configuration of the Cu²⁺ ion and state the number of unpaired electrons it has.
parts.answer: [Ar] 3d⁹; one unpaired electron

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why, when a transition element forms a positive ion, the 4s electrons are removed before the 3d electrons.
parts.answer: Once the 3d orbitals are occupied, the 4s electrons are higher in energy (further out) than the 3d electrons, so they are lost first.
parts.working: B1 4s is higher in energy / outermost once 3d filled

parts.label: a
parts.text: An ion Z³⁺ has the configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁵. Identify element Z.
parts.answer: Iron (Fe)

parts.label: b
parts.text: An ion W²⁺ has the configuration [Ar] 3d¹⁰. Identify W and explain why W²⁺ is colourless in solution.
parts.answer: Zinc; the 3d sub-shell is full so no d–d electron transitions are possible.
parts.working:
B1 zinc
B1 full 3d / no d–d transitions

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the block of the Periodic Table to which selenium belongs and write the configuration of the Se²⁻ ion.
parts.answer: p-block; [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p⁶ (same as krypton)

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which pair of ions has the same number of unpaired electrons?
A Fe²⁺ and Co²⁺
B Mn²⁺ and Fe³⁺
C Cu⁺ and Cu²⁺
D Ni²⁺ and Ti³⁺
parts.answer: B Mn²⁺ and Fe³⁺
parts.working: Mn²⁺ and Fe³⁺ are both [Ar] 3d⁵ with five unpaired electrons. Fe²⁺ 3d⁶ has 4 but Co²⁺ 3d⁷ has 3; Cu⁺ 3d¹⁰ has 0, Cu²⁺ 3d⁹ has 1; Ni²⁺ 3d⁸ has 2, Ti³⁺ 3d¹ has 1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why atomic radius decreases from sodium to chlorine across Period 3.
parts.answer: Nuclear charge increases while electrons are added to the same shell with similar shielding, so outer electrons are pulled closer.
parts.working:
M1 increasing nuclear charge / more protons
M2 same shell / similar shielding, so stronger attraction

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why atomic radius increases down Group 1 from lithium to caesium.
parts.answer: Each element has an extra occupied shell, so outer electrons are further from the nucleus and more shielded.
parts.working:
M1 more shells
M2 more shielding (outweighs increased nuclear charge)

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what is meant by an isoelectronic series and give the electronic configuration shared by all six ions.
parts.answer: Species with the same number of electrons (same configuration); 1s² 2s² 2p⁶
parts.working:
B1 same number of electrons
B1 1s² 2s² 2p⁶

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain the trend in ionic radius shown in the table.
parts.answer: Proton number increases from N (7) to Al (13) while the number of electrons stays at 10, so the electrons are attracted more strongly and pulled closer.
parts.working:
M1 same number of electrons / same shielding
M2 increasing nuclear charge pulls electrons closer

parts.label: a
parts.text: Place the species S²⁻, Cl⁻, Ar and K⁺ in order of decreasing radius.
parts.answer: S²⁻ > Cl⁻ > Ar > K⁺

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why S²⁻ is the largest of these species.
parts.answer: All have 18 electrons, but S²⁻ has the fewest protons (16), so the attraction of its nucleus for the electrons is weakest.
parts.working:
M1 same number of electrons (18)
M2 fewest protons so weakest attraction

stem: Radii (nm): Na atom 0.186, Na⁺ 0.102, Cl atom 0.099, Cl⁻ 0.181

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the percentage change in radius when (i) a sodium atom forms Na⁺ and (ii) a chlorine atom forms Cl⁻. Give each to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why Na⁺ is much smaller than a Na atom.
parts.answer: Na⁺ has lost its only 3s electron, so it has one fewer shell; the remaining 10 electrons are attracted by 11 protons.
parts.working:
M1 loses the outer (third) shell
M2 more protons than electrons so electrons pulled in more strongly / less repulsion

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why Cl⁻ is much larger than a Cl atom.
parts.answer: The extra electron increases repulsion between electrons in the same shell, while the nuclear charge is unchanged, so the electron cloud expands.
parts.working: B1 extra electron, more repulsion, same nuclear charge

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe the shapes of an s orbital and a p orbital.
parts.answer: s: spherical. p: dumbbell (two lobes on opposite sides of the nucleus).

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the number of orbitals in a 3d sub-shell.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the maximum number of electrons that the third shell (n = 3) can hold.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain what is meant by Hund's rule and use it to describe how the three 2p electrons are arranged in a nitrogen atom.
parts.answer: Electrons occupy orbitals of equal energy singly, with parallel spins, before pairing; nitrogen has one electron in each of 2px, 2py and 2pz.
parts.working:
M1 orbitals of same energy filled singly before pairing
M2 one electron in each 2p orbital, parallel spins

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the number of unpaired electrons in atoms of phosphorus, sulfur and chlorine.
parts.answer: P 3, S 2, Cl 1
parts.working: B2 all three; B1 two correct

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the 4s sub-shell fills before the 3d sub-shell in potassium and calcium.
parts.answer: In these atoms the 4s sub-shell is lower in energy than the 3d sub-shell.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
How many orbitals are fully occupied (contain two electrons) in a ground-state sulfur atom?
A 6
B 7
C 8
D 9
parts.answer: B 7
parts.working: S is 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁴: 1s, 2s, three 2p and 3s are full (6) and the 3p⁴ has one full orbital and two half-filled, giving 7. Answer A forgets the paired 3p orbital.

stem: Hydrogen and iodine react in a sealed flask: H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g). At 700 K the equilibrium concentrations are [H₂] = 0.0040 mol/dm³, [I₂] = 0.0025 mol/dm³ and [HI] = 0.0230 mol/dm³.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write an expression for Kc for this reaction.
parts.answer: Kc = [HI]² / ([H₂][I₂])

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the value of Kc at this temperature. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why Kc for this reaction has no units.
parts.answer: There are equal numbers of moles of gas (concentration terms) on each side, so the units cancel.

author: HomiLabs

stem:
A student in Karachi mixes 1.00 mol of ethanoic acid with 1.20 mol of ethanol and a few drops of concentrated sulfuric acid, then leaves the mixture in a sealed flask until equilibrium is reached:
CH₃COOH(l) + C₂H₅OH(l) ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅(l) + H₂O(l)
At equilibrium, 0.72 mol of ethyl ethanoate is present.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the amounts, in mol, of ethanoic acid, ethanol and water present at equilibrium.
parts.answer: ethanoic acid 0.28 mol; ethanol 0.48 mol; water 0.72 mol
parts.working:
M1 0.72 mol of each reactant used
A1 all three amounts

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate Kc. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the total volume of the mixture is not needed to calculate Kc for this reaction.
parts.answer: The volume terms cancel because there are equal numbers of moles on each side of the equation.

author: HomiLabs

stem: 1.00 mol of dinitrogen tetroxide is heated in a closed container: N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g). At equilibrium, 25.0% of the N₂O₄ has dissociated and the total pressure is 150 kPa.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the amount of each gas at equilibrium and the mole fraction of each gas.
parts.answer: N₂O₄ 0.75 mol, NO₂ 0.50 mol; mole fractions 0.60 and 0.40
parts.working:
M1 amounts
A1 mole fractions (total 1.25 mol)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the partial pressure of each gas.
parts.answer: p(N₂O₄) = 90 kPa; p(NO₂) = 60 kPa

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write an expression for Kp and calculate its value, giving its units.
parts.answer: Kp = p(NO₂)²/p(N₂O₄) = 40.0 kPa

author: HomiLabs

stem: A mixture of nitrogen and hydrogen is allowed to reach equilibrium at a fixed temperature: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g). At equilibrium the mixture contains 2.40 mol N₂, 7.20 mol H₂ and 1.60 mol NH₃, and the total pressure is 2.00 × 10⁴ kPa.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the amounts of nitrogen and hydrogen that were present at the start.
parts.answer: N₂ 3.20 mol; H₂ 9.60 mol
parts.working:
M1 1.60 mol NH₃ formed needs 0.80 mol N₂ and 2.40 mol H₂
A1 both

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the partial pressure of each gas at equilibrium.
parts.answer: p(N₂) = 4.29 × 10³ kPa; p(H₂) = 1.29 × 10⁴ kPa; p(NH₃) = 2.86 × 10³ kPa
parts.working:
M1 mole fractions (total 11.2 mol)
A1 all three

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate Kp and give its units.
parts.answer: Kp = 8.96 × 10⁻¹⁰ kPa⁻²
parts.working:
M1 Kp = p(NH₃)² / (p(N₂) × p(H₂)³)
A1 8.96 × 10⁻¹⁰ kPa⁻²

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text:
0.200 mol of PCl₅ is heated in a sealed 2.00 dm³ vessel. At equilibrium 40.0% of the PCl₅ has dissociated: PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g). What is the value of Kc, in mol/dm³?
A 0.0267
B 0.0533
C 0.107
D 0.0133
parts.working: At equilibrium: PCl₅ 0.120 mol, PCl₃ 0.080 mol, Cl₂ 0.080 mol; concentrations 0.060, 0.040, 0.040 mol/dm³. Kc = 0.040 × 0.040 / 0.060 = 0.0267. B uses amounts instead of concentrations.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write an expression for the ionic product of water, Kw, and state its value at 298 K.
parts.answer: Kw = [H⁺][OH⁻] = 1.00 × 10⁻¹⁴ mol² dm⁻⁶

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the pH of 0.0250 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the pH of 0.0150 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide solution at 298 K.

stem: Propanoic acid, used as a food preservative, has Ka = 1.35 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³ at 298 K.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write an expression for the acid dissociation constant, Ka, of propanoic acid, CH₃CH₂COOH.
parts.answer: Ka = [CH₃CH₂COO⁻][H⁺] / [CH₃CH₂COOH]

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the pH of 0.100 mol/dm³ propanoic acid. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State two assumptions you made in (b).
parts.answer: [H⁺] = [CH₃CH₂COO⁻] (H⁺ from water ignored); the equilibrium concentration of the acid equals 0.100 (dissociation is negligible).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Calculate pKa for propanoic acid.

author: HomiLabs

stem: Methanoic acid occurs in ant and nettle stings. A 0.200 mol/dm³ solution of methanoic acid has pH 2.22 at 298 K.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate [H⁺] in the solution.
parts.answer: 6.03 × 10⁻³ mol/dm³

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate Ka for methanoic acid. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
parts.answer: 1.82 × 10⁻⁴ mol/dm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why methanoic acid is described as a weak acid.
parts.answer: It only partially dissociates (ionises) in water.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: 25.0 cm³ of 0.120 mol/dm³ HCl is mixed with 20.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ NaOH. Calculate the pH of the resulting solution.

parts.label: b
parts.text: At 50 °C, Kw = 5.48 × 10⁻¹⁴ mol² dm⁻⁶. Calculate the pH of pure water at 50 °C.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why pure water at 50 °C is neutral even though its pH is below 7.
parts.answer: [H⁺] = [OH⁻] in pure water.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Use the data to deduce whether the dissociation of water is exothermic or endothermic.
parts.answer: Endothermic: Kw increases as temperature increases.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the pH of 0.00500 mol/dm³ sulfuric acid, assuming it is fully dissociated into 2H⁺ and SO₄²⁻.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the pH of 0.00500 mol/dm³ ethanoic acid (Ka = 1.74 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the volume of 0.0100 mol/dm³ NaOH needed to neutralise 25.0 cm³ of each acid.
parts.answer: sulfuric acid 25.0 cm³; ethanoic acid 12.5 cm³

parts.label: d
parts.text: Explain why the volume of NaOH needed to neutralise the ethanoic acid depends on its full concentration, even though only a small fraction of the acid is dissociated.
parts.answer: As OH⁻ removes H⁺, the equilibrium CH₃COOH ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺ shifts right until all the acid has reacted.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write an expression for the solubility product of calcium fluoride, CaF₂, and give its units.
parts.answer: Ksp = [Ca²⁺][F⁻]²; mol³ dm⁻⁹

parts.label: b
parts.text: Ksp of CaF₂ is 3.9 × 10⁻¹¹ mol³ dm⁻⁹ at 298 K. Calculate the solubility of CaF₂ in mol/dm³.
parts.answer: 2.1 × 10⁻⁴ mol/dm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: Convert your answer to (b) into g/dm³. [Mr: CaF₂, 78.1]
parts.answer: 0.017 g/dm³

stem: A saturated solution of magnesium hydroxide at 298 K contains 9.6 × 10⁻³ g of dissolved Mg(OH)₂ per dm³.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the solubility of Mg(OH)₂ in mol/dm³. [Mr: Mg(OH)₂, 58.3]
parts.answer: 1.65 × 10⁻⁴ mol/dm³

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate Ksp for Mg(OH)₂, giving units.
parts.answer: 1.79 × 10⁻¹¹ mol³ dm⁻⁹
parts.working:
M1 Ksp = s × (2s)² = 4s³
A1 value and units

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest why milk of magnesia (a suspension of Mg(OH)₂) dissolves in stomach acid even though Mg(OH)₂ is almost insoluble in water.
parts.answer: H⁺ ions react with OH⁻ ions, lowering [OH⁻]; the ionic product falls below Ksp, so more solid dissolves (equilibrium shifts right).
parts.working:
M1 H⁺ removes OH⁻
M2 Mg(OH)₂ ⇌ Mg²⁺ + 2OH⁻ shifts right / ionic product below Ksp

author: HomiLabs

stem: Ksp of silver chloride, AgCl, is 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰ mol² dm⁻⁶ at 298 K.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the solubility of AgCl, in mol/dm³, in pure water.
parts.answer: 1.3 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the solubility of AgCl, in mol/dm³, in 0.050 mol/dm³ sodium chloride solution.
parts.answer: 3.6 × 10⁻⁹ mol/dm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the effect shown by your answers and explain it.
parts.answer: Common ion effect: the added Cl⁻ shifts AgCl(s) ⇌ Ag⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) to the left, so less AgCl dissolves.
parts.working:
B1 common ion effect
B1 equilibrium shifts left / [Ag⁺] must fall to keep product = Ksp

author: HomiLabs

stem: Ksp of barium sulfate is 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁰ mol² dm⁻⁶ at 298 K. 100 cm³ of 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ mol/dm³ barium chloride is mixed with 150 cm³ of 2.0 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³ sodium sulfate.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the concentrations of Ba²⁺ and SO₄²⁻ in the mixture immediately after mixing.
parts.answer: [Ba²⁺] = 4.0 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³; [SO₄²⁻] = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³
parts.working:
M1 dilution by total volume 250 cm³
A1 both

parts.label: b
parts.text: Deduce whether a precipitate of barium sulfate forms. Show your reasoning.
parts.answer: Ionic product = 4.8 × 10⁻¹⁰ mol² dm⁻⁶, which is greater than Ksp (1.1 × 10⁻¹⁰), so a precipitate forms.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A groundwater sample contains 0.010 mol/dm³ sulfate ions. Calculate the maximum concentration of Ba²⁺ that can be present without precipitation.
parts.answer: 1.1 × 10⁻⁸ mol/dm³

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what is meant by a buffer solution.
parts.answer: A solution that resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or alkali are added.
parts.working:
M1 resists change in pH
M2 small amounts of acid or alkali

parts.label: b
parts.text: A buffer contains ethanoic acid and sodium ethanoate. Write equations to show how it removes added H⁺ ions and added OH⁻ ions.
parts.answer: CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺ → CH₃COOH; CH₃COOH + OH⁻ → CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why a solution of ethanoic acid alone is a poor buffer.
parts.answer: It contains very little CH₃COO⁻ (weak acid barely dissociated), so it cannot remove added H⁺.

stem: A buffer is made containing 0.150 mol/dm³ ethanoic acid and 0.250 mol/dm³ sodium ethanoate. Ka of ethanoic acid = 1.74 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the pH of the buffer. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State how the composition of the buffer could be changed to give a buffer with a lower pH.
parts.answer: Increase the ratio [CH₃COOH]/[CH₃COO⁻] (more acid or less salt).

author: HomiLabs

stem: A buffer of total volume 1.00 dm³ contains 0.100 mol of ethanoic acid and 0.0800 mol of sodium ethanoate. Ka of ethanoic acid = 1.74 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the pH of the buffer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: 0.0100 mol of solid NaOH is dissolved in the buffer. Calculate the new pH. Assume the volume does not change.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the pH if the same 0.0100 mol of NaOH were dissolved in 1.00 dm³ of pure water instead, and comment.
parts.answer: 12.00; the pH rises by about 5 units, compared with about 0.1 in the buffer.
parts.working:
B1 12.00
B1 comment on buffer resisting change

author: HomiLabs

stem: Blood plasma is buffered mainly by carbonic acid and hydrogencarbonate ions: H₂CO₃ ⇌ H⁺ + HCO₃⁻, Ka = 7.9 × 10⁻⁷ mol/dm³ at body temperature.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write an equation to show how this buffer removes excess H⁺ ions produced during exercise.
parts.answer: HCO₃⁻ + H⁺ → H₂CO₃

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the ratio [HCO₃⁻] : [H₂CO₃] in blood at pH 7.40. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest why a high ratio of HCO₃⁻ to H₂CO₃ is useful in the body.
parts.answer: Metabolism mainly produces acids (e.g. CO₂, lactic acid), so a large reserve of HCO₃⁻ is needed to remove H⁺.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text:
2NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g)   ΔH = −57 kJ/mol
Which change increases the equilibrium yield of N₂O₄?
A increasing the temperature
B decreasing the pressure
C increasing the pressure
D adding a catalyst
parts.answer: C increasing the pressure
parts.working: Increasing pressure favours the side with fewer moles of gas (1 mol N₂O₄ vs 2 mol NO₂). Increasing temperature favours the endothermic (backward) reaction; a catalyst does not change the position of equilibrium.

stem:
In aqueous solution the following equilibrium is set up:
[Co(H₂O)₆]²⁺ (pink) + 4Cl⁻ ⇌ [CoCl₄]²⁻ (blue) + 6H₂O   ΔH positive

parts.label: a
parts.text: State and explain the colour change seen when concentrated hydrochloric acid is added to the pink solution.
parts.answer: Turns blue; adding Cl⁻ increases [Cl⁻], so the equilibrium shifts to the right to remove Cl⁻.
parts.working:
B1 blue
B1 shifts right to oppose increase in [Cl⁻]

parts.label: b
parts.text: The blue solution is placed in an ice bath. State and explain what is seen.
parts.answer: Turns pink; lowering temperature favours the exothermic direction, which is the backward reaction.
parts.working:
B1 pink
B1 forward is endothermic so equilibrium shifts left on cooling

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the effect of adding water to the blue solution.
parts.answer: It turns pink (equilibrium shifts left).

author: HomiLabs

stem:
Methanol is made industrially from synthesis gas:
CO(g) + 2H₂(g) ⇌ CH₃OH(g)   ΔH = −91 kJ/mol

parts.label: a
parts.text: State and explain the effect of increasing the pressure on the equilibrium yield of methanol.
parts.answer: Yield increases; the equilibrium shifts to the right, the side with fewer moles of gas (1 mol vs 3 mol).
parts.working:
B1 increases
B1 fewer gas moles on right

parts.label: b
parts.text: State and explain the effect of increasing the temperature on the equilibrium yield of methanol.
parts.answer: Yield decreases; the forward reaction is exothermic, so the equilibrium shifts left to absorb heat.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A copper-based catalyst is used. State its effect on the rate and on the position of equilibrium.
parts.answer: Increases the rate of both forward and backward reactions equally; no effect on the position of equilibrium (equilibrium reached faster).

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text:
H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g)   ΔH = −9.6 kJ/mol
An equilibrium mixture of the three gases, which is purple because of I₂, is compressed to half its volume at constant temperature. Which statement is correct?
A The position of equilibrium is unchanged but the purple colour becomes darker.
B The position of equilibrium moves to the right and the purple colour becomes paler.
C The value of Kc doubles.
D The position of equilibrium moves to the left and the purple colour becomes darker.
parts.answer: A The position of equilibrium is unchanged but the purple colour becomes darker.
parts.working: There are 2 mol of gas on each side, so pressure does not affect the position of equilibrium and Kc depends only on temperature. Halving the volume doubles the concentration of I₂, so the colour darkens. B wrongly assumes fewer gas moles on the right.

stem: Iodine is shaken with hexane and water until equilibrium is reached at 25 °C. The concentration of iodine is 0.0425 mol/dm³ in the hexane layer and 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ mol/dm³ in the water layer.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what is meant by the partition coefficient, Kpc.
parts.answer: The ratio of the concentrations of a solute in two immiscible solvents when the system is at equilibrium.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate Kpc for iodine between hexane and water.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest why Kpc is much greater than 1 for iodine in this system.
parts.answer: I₂ is non-polar, so it dissolves much better in non-polar hexane than in polar water.

author: HomiLabs

stem: An organic compound Q is extracted from a plant sample in Swat. 2.50 g of Q is dissolved in 100 cm³ of water. The solution is shaken with 20.0 cm³ of dichloromethane. Kpc for Q (dichloromethane/water) = 15.0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the mass of Q extracted into the dichloromethane. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State one property that the extracting solvent must have.
parts.answer: It must be immiscible with water (and Q must be more soluble in it).

author: HomiLabs

stem: 1.00 g of compound Q is dissolved in 100 cm³ of water. Kpc for Q between ethoxyethane and water is 4.0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the mass of Q extracted by one portion of 50 cm³ of ethoxyethane.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the total mass of Q extracted using two successive portions of 25 cm³ of ethoxyethane.
parts.working:
M1 first portion: (x/25)/((1.00 − x)/100) = 4.0 so x = 0.500 g
M1 second portion removes half of the remaining 0.500 g = 0.250 g
A1 total 0.750 g

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the conclusion that can be drawn from your answers.
parts.answer: Several small extractions remove more solute than one extraction with the same total volume.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text:
When pure nitric acid and pure sulfuric acid are mixed, this equilibrium is set up:
HNO₃ + H₂SO₄ ⇌ H₂NO₃⁺ + HSO₄⁻
Which species in the forward reaction acts as a Brønsted–Lowry base?
A HNO₃
B H₂SO₄
C H₂NO₃⁺
D HSO₄⁻
parts.answer: A HNO₃
parts.working: HNO₃ accepts a proton from H₂SO₄ to form H₂NO₃⁺, so HNO₃ is the base. H₂SO₄ donates the proton (acid); HSO₄⁻ is the conjugate base, acting as a base only in the reverse reaction.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In the reaction NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻, identify the two conjugate acid–base pairs.
parts.answer: NH₄⁺/NH₃ and H₂O/OH⁻

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write two equations to show that the hydrogencarbonate ion, HCO₃⁻, can act both as a Brønsted–Lowry acid and as a Brønsted–Lowry base.
parts.answer: Acid: HCO₃⁻ + OH⁻ → CO₃²⁻ + H₂O; base: HCO₃⁻ + H⁺ → H₂CO₃ (→ H₂O + CO₂)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Separate 50.0 cm³ samples of 0.100 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid and 0.100 mol/dm³ ethanoic acid react with excess magnesium ribbon. Calculate the volume of hydrogen, in cm³ at room conditions, produced by each, and explain why the rates of reaction differ. [1 mol gas occupies 24.0 dm³]
parts.answer: 60.0 cm³ each; HCl is a strong acid (fully dissociated) so [H⁺] is higher and it reacts faster; ethanoic acid is weak and partly dissociated, but equilibrium shifts as H⁺ is used, so it gives the same total volume.
parts.working:
B1 60.0 cm³
B1 HCl fully dissociated → higher [H⁺] → faster
B1 ethanoic acid partial dissociation; all eventually reacts so same volume

parts.label: a
parts.text: State two features of a reaction mixture at dynamic equilibrium.
parts.answer: The rates of the forward and backward reactions are equal; the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why a dynamic equilibrium can only be set up in a closed system.
parts.answer: No substances can enter or leave, so the backward reaction can occur (products are not lost).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calcium carbonate is heated in an open crucible in a lime kiln. Explain why it decomposes completely rather than reaching equilibrium: CaCO₃(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO₂(g).
parts.answer: CO₂ escapes, so the backward reaction cannot take place.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which statement about a reversible reaction at dynamic equilibrium is always correct?
A The concentrations of reactants and products are equal.
B The forward and backward reactions have stopped.
C The rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the backward reaction.
D The amount of products is greater than the amount of reactants.
parts.answer: C The rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the backward reaction.
parts.working: At dynamic equilibrium both reactions continue at equal rates, so concentrations stay constant, but not necessarily equal. A confuses constant with equal.

stem:
In the Contact process, sulfur trioxide is made from sulfur dioxide:
2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g)   ΔH = −197 kJ/mol

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the catalyst and typical temperature used in this stage of the Contact process.
parts.answer: Vanadium(V) oxide, V₂O₅; about 450 °C

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why a pressure of only 1–2 atm is used even though a higher pressure would increase the equilibrium yield.
parts.answer: Conversion is already very high (over 95%) at low pressure, so the extra cost of high-pressure plant and energy is not justified.
parts.working:
M1 high conversion already
M2 high pressure expensive / not economic

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the mass, in tonnes, of SO₃ formed from 1.00 tonne of SO₂ if 98.0% of the SO₂ is converted. Give your answer to 3 significant figures. [Mr: SO₂, 64.1; SO₃, 80.1]
parts.answer: 1.22 tonnes

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why but-2-ene, CH₃CH=CHCH₃, shows cis/trans (geometrical) isomerism.
parts.answer: There is no rotation about the C=C double bond (π bond), and each carbon of the C=C carries two different groups (H and CH₃).
parts.working:
M1 restricted rotation about C=C / π bond
M2 each C of the C=C has two different groups

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe the difference between cis-but-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene.
parts.answer: In the cis isomer both CH₃ groups are on the same side of the double bond; in the trans isomer they are on opposite sides.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why but-1-ene, CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃, does not show cis/trans isomerism.
parts.answer: One carbon of the C=C carries two identical groups (two H atoms).

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which compound shows cis/trans isomerism?
A CH₂=CHCH₃
B (CH₃)₂C=CHCH₃
C CH₃CH=CHCl
D CH₂=CCl₂
parts.answer: C CH₃CH=CHCl
parts.working: In CH₃CH=CHCl each carbon of the C=C has two different groups (CH₃/H and Cl/H). In each of the others, one carbon of the C=C carries two identical groups.

stem: 1,2-dichloroethene, ClCH=CHCl, exists as cis and trans isomers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe, in words, the arrangement of the atoms in each isomer.
parts.answer: cis: both Cl atoms on the same side of the C=C (and both H atoms on the other side); trans: the Cl atoms on opposite sides. All six atoms lie in one plane.
parts.working:
B1 cis description
B1 trans description

parts.label: b
parts.text: The boiling points are 60 °C and 48 °C. Deduce which isomer has the higher boiling point and explain.
parts.answer: cis (60 °C). The cis molecule is polar because its C–Cl dipoles do not cancel, so it has permanent dipole–permanent dipole forces as well as London dispersion forces. In the trans isomer the dipoles cancel, so it is non-polar.
parts.working:
B1 cis higher
M1 cis has a net dipole / permanent dipole–dipole forces
M1 trans dipoles cancel (symmetrical), only London forces

author: HomiLabs

stem: Pent-3-en-2-ol has the structural formula CH₃CH(OH)CH=CHCH₃.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Identify the chiral centre in pent-3-en-2-ol.
parts.answer: Carbon-2 (the carbon bonded to OH, H, CH₃ and CH=CHCH₃).

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the two types of stereoisomerism shown by this compound.
parts.answer: Optical isomerism and cis/trans (geometrical) isomerism.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Deduce the total number of stereoisomers of pent-3-en-2-ol. Explain your answer.
parts.working:
M1 two forms about the C=C × two enantiomers at C-2
A1 2 × 2 = 4

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which compound shows optical isomerism but not cis/trans isomerism?
A CH₃CHBrCH₂CH₃
B CH₃CH=CHCH₃
C CH₃CH₂CH₂Br
D CH₃CH=CHCH(OH)CH₃
parts.answer: A CH₃CHBrCH₂CH₃
parts.working: 2-bromobutane has a carbon bonded to four different groups (H, Br, CH₃, C₂H₅) and no C=C. D shows both types; B shows only cis/trans; C shows neither.

stem: Pentan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₂CH₃, is heated with concentrated phosphoric acid. Three different alkenes, each C₅H₁₀, are formed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the three alkenes formed and give their structural formulae.
parts.answer: pent-1-ene CH₂=CHCH₂CH₂CH₃; cis-pent-2-ene and trans-pent-2-ene, both CH₃CH=CHCH₂CH₃
parts.working:
B1 pent-1-ene
B1 pent-2-ene
B1 cis and trans identified as the two forms of pent-2-ene

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the relationship between two of the products and explain why they are different compounds.
parts.answer: cis-pent-2-ene and trans-pent-2-ene are stereoisomers (geometrical isomers): same structural formula but different arrangement in space; they cannot interconvert because there is no rotation about the C=C.
parts.working:
M1 cis/trans (stereo) isomers
M2 restricted rotation about C=C

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why pentan-3-ol, CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₂CH₃, gives only two alkene products when dehydrated in the same way.
parts.answer: Loss of H from either neighbouring carbon gives the same structure, pent-2-ene, which exists as cis and trans forms.

author: HomiLabs

stem: Butenedioic acid, HOOC–CH=CH–COOH, has a cis isomer (maleic acid) and a trans isomer (fumaric acid). Fumaric acid is used as a food acidity regulator.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe the difference in structure between the two isomers.
parts.answer: In maleic acid (cis) both COOH groups are on the same side of the C=C; in fumaric acid (trans) they are on opposite sides.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Fumaric acid melts at 287 °C but maleic acid melts at 135 °C. Suggest an explanation.
parts.answer: Fumaric acid molecules are more symmetrical and pack more closely in the lattice and form hydrogen bonds between molecules in all directions. In maleic acid the two COOH groups are close enough to form an intramolecular hydrogen bond, leaving fewer intermolecular hydrogen bonds, and the molecules pack less well.
parts.working:
M1 trans packs better / more symmetrical
M1 intermolecular hydrogen bonding in fumaric acid
M1 cis forms intramolecular hydrogen bond, so fewer intermolecular

parts.label: c
parts.text: On heating, maleic acid loses water to form a cyclic anhydride, but fumaric acid does not. Suggest why.
parts.answer: Only in the cis isomer are the two COOH groups close enough to react with each other.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Name these compounds:
(i) CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃
(ii) CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₃
(iii) CH₃COCH₂CH₃
(iv) CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂Cl
parts.answer: (i) 2-methylbutane (ii) butan-2-ol (iii) butanone (iv) 1-chlorobutane

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the structural formula of 3-methylpentan-2-one.
parts.answer: CH₃COCH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the structural formulae and names of the three structural isomers of C₅H₁₂.
parts.answer: pentane CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃; 2-methylbutane CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃; 2,2-dimethylpropane C(CH₃)₄

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the type of structural isomerism shown.
parts.answer: Chain isomerism

parts.label: c
parts.text: Their boiling points are 36 °C, 28 °C and 10 °C. Match each value to an isomer and explain the trend.
parts.answer: pentane 36 °C, 2-methylbutane 28 °C, 2,2-dimethylpropane 10 °C; more branching gives a more compact shape with less surface contact, so weaker London dispersion forces.
parts.working:
B1 matching
B1 branching → less surface contact → weaker London forces

parts.label: a
parts.text:
How many structural isomers have the molecular formula C₄H₉Br?
A 2
B 3
C 4
D 5
parts.answer: C 4
parts.working: 1-bromobutane, 2-bromobutane, 1-bromo-2-methylpropane and 2-bromo-2-methylpropane. Optical isomers of 2-bromobutane are stereoisomers, not structural isomers, so 5 is wrong.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the four alcohols with molecular formula C₄H₁₀O and classify each as primary, secondary or tertiary.
parts.answer: butan-1-ol (primary); butan-2-ol (secondary); 2-methylpropan-1-ol (primary); 2-methylpropan-2-ol (tertiary)
parts.working: B1 each name with correct class

parts.label: b
parts.text: Ethoxyethane, CH₃CH₂OCH₂CH₃, also has the formula C₄H₁₀O. State the type of isomerism between ethoxyethane and butan-1-ol.
parts.answer: Functional group isomerism

parts.label: a
parts.text:
State the type of structural isomerism shown by each pair:
(i) butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol
(ii) pentane and 2-methylbutane
(iii) propanal and propanone
(iv) ethanoic acid and methyl methanoate
parts.answer: (i) positional (ii) chain (iii) functional group (iv) functional group

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give the structural formulae and names of the two esters with molecular formula C₃H₆O₂.
parts.answer: methyl ethanoate CH₃COOCH₃; ethyl methanoate HCOOCH₂CH₃

parts.label: a
parts.text:
What is the systematic name of CH₃CH(C₂H₅)CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₃?
A 2-ethyl-4-methylpentane
B 2,4-dimethylhexane
C 3,5-dimethylhexane
D 4-ethyl-2-methylpentane
parts.answer: B 2,4-dimethylhexane
parts.working: The longest chain (6 C) runs through the ethyl group. Numbering from the end nearer the branches puts methyl groups on C-2 and C-4. A and D do not use the longest chain; C numbers from the wrong end.

parts.label: a
parts.text: There are eight alcohols with formula C₅H₁₂O. Name the only tertiary alcohol.
parts.answer: 2-methylbutan-2-ol

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the three secondary alcohols with formula C₅H₁₂O.
parts.answer: pentan-2-ol; pentan-3-ol; 3-methylbutan-2-ol

parts.label: c
parts.text: Which of the secondary alcohols in (b) are chiral? Explain why the other is not.
parts.answer: pentan-2-ol and 3-methylbutan-2-ol are chiral; pentan-3-ol is not, because its C-3 carries two identical ethyl groups.
parts.working:
B1 both chiral ones
B1 pentan-3-ol has two identical C₂H₅ groups

stem: Lactic acid (2-hydroxypropanoic acid), CH₃CH(OH)COOH, is formed when milk is turned into yoghurt (dahi).

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what is meant by a chiral centre.
parts.answer: A carbon atom bonded to four different atoms or groups.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Identify the chiral centre in lactic acid and name the four groups attached to it.
parts.answer: The central carbon, C-2; it carries H, OH, CH₃ and COOH.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State how the two optical isomers of lactic acid are related, and how they could be distinguished.
parts.answer: They are non-superimposable mirror images (enantiomers); they rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions (by equal amounts).
parts.working:
B1 non-superimposable mirror images
B1 rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which compound has a chiral centre?
A CH₃CH(OH)CH₃
B CH₃CH₂CHClCH₃
C (CH₃)₃CBr
D ClCH₂CH₂Cl
parts.answer: B CH₃CH₂CHClCH₃
parts.working: In CH₃CH₂CHClCH₃ the C-2 carries H, Cl, CH₃ and C₂H₅. In propan-2-ol C-2 carries two CH₃ groups, so it is not chiral.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Identify the chiral centres in 3-methylpentan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃.
parts.answer: C-2 and C-3

parts.label: b
parts.text: Deduce the maximum number of stereoisomers of this compound.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A sample containing equal amounts of the two enantiomers of a chiral compound has no effect on plane-polarised light. State the name of such a mixture and explain this observation.
parts.answer: Racemic mixture; the rotations caused by the two enantiomers are equal and opposite, so they cancel.
parts.working:
B1 racemic
B1 equal and opposite rotations cancel

stem: Ethanal, CH₃CHO, reacts with HCN in the presence of a small amount of KCN in a nucleophilic addition reaction.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the product and identify its chiral centre.
parts.answer: 2-hydroxypropanenitrile, CH₃CH(OH)CN; the carbon bonded to H, OH, CH₃ and CN

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the product obtained is not optically active.
parts.answer: The C=O group and the atoms around it are planar (trigonal planar carbonyl carbon). The CN⁻ nucleophile can attack from either side of the plane with equal probability, giving equal amounts of the two enantiomers: a racemic mixture, whose rotations cancel.
parts.working:
M1 carbonyl group planar
M1 attack equally likely from above and below
M1 racemic mixture formed, rotations cancel

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Alanine, CH₃CH(NH₂)COOH, is an amino acid. Explain why it has two optical isomers.
parts.answer: It has a carbon atom bonded to four different groups (H, NH₂, CH₃, COOH).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Many drugs are chiral, but often only one enantiomer is effective. Suggest two reasons why a drug company may choose to produce only the active enantiomer.
parts.answer: Smaller dose needed (half the mass is not wasted); the other enantiomer may have harmful side effects or no effect; reduced cost of purification/regulatory problems.
parts.working: B1 each for two of: smaller dose / less waste; other enantiomer may be harmful; fewer side effects

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why enantiomers can have different effects in the body although their physical and chemical properties are almost identical.
parts.answer: Receptors and enzymes in the body are themselves chiral, so only one enantiomer fits the binding site.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Classify each reaction as addition, substitution, elimination or hydrolysis:
(i) C₂H₄ + Br₂ → CH₂BrCH₂Br
(ii) CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl
(iii) C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O (with hot Al₂O₃)
(iv) CH₃COOCH₃ + H₂O → CH₃COOH + CH₃OH
parts.answer: (i) addition (ii) substitution (iii) elimination (iv) hydrolysis

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which species can act as a nucleophile?
A H⁺
B NO₂⁺
C CN⁻
D Br•
parts.answer: C CN⁻
parts.working: A nucleophile donates a lone pair of electrons to an electron-deficient carbon. CN⁻ has a lone pair (on carbon). H⁺ and NO₂⁺ are electrophiles; Br• is a free radical.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain the difference between homolytic and heterolytic fission of a covalent bond.
parts.answer: Homolytic: each atom takes one electron of the bonding pair, forming two free radicals. Heterolytic: one atom takes both electrons, forming a positive and a negative ion.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write an equation for the homolytic fission of chlorine in ultraviolet light.
parts.answer: Cl₂ → 2Cl•

parts.label: c
parts.text: Define the term electrophile.
parts.answer: A species that accepts a pair of electrons (to form a new covalent bond).

stem: Ethane reacts with chlorine in sunlight by free-radical substitution.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the two propagation steps for the formation of chloroethane.
parts.answer:
C₂H₆ + Cl• → C₂H₅• + HCl
C₂H₅• + Cl₂ → C₂H₅Cl + Cl•

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write an equation for a termination step that forms a hydrocarbon with four carbon atoms.
parts.answer: 2C₂H₅• → C₄H₁₀

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the reaction gives a mixture of products such as C₂H₄Cl₂ and C₂H₃Cl₃ as well as chloroethane.
parts.answer: Cl• can also remove H from chloroethane (further substitution), and the radicals formed react with Cl₂.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which functional group is present in CH₃CH₂COOCH₃?
A ester
B carboxylic acid
C ketone
D ether
parts.answer: A ester
parts.working: –COO– joining two carbon chains is an ester (methyl propanoate). A carboxylic acid needs –COOH with an O–H.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the four functional groups present in compound J, HOCH₂CH=CHCOCH₂CH₂CHO.
parts.answer: primary alcohol (hydroxy); alkene; ketone; aldehyde

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the molecular formula of J.
parts.answer: C₇H₁₀O₃

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Classify each compound as primary, secondary or tertiary:
(i) (CH₃)₃COH
(ii) CH₃CH(OH)CH₃
(iii) CH₃CH₂CH₂Br
(iv) (CH₃)₂CHCH₂Cl
parts.answer: (i) tertiary alcohol (ii) secondary alcohol (iii) primary halogenoalkane (iv) primary halogenoalkane

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain how you classified (iv).
parts.answer: The carbon bonded to Cl is bonded to only one other carbon atom.

stem: Citral, (CH₃)₂C=CHCH₂CH₂C(CH₃)=CHCHO, gives lemongrass its smell.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the functional groups present in citral.
parts.answer: Alkene (two C=C) and aldehyde

parts.label: b
parts.text: Deduce the molecular formula of citral and calculate its Mr. [Ar: C, 12.0; H, 1.0; O, 16.0]
parts.answer: C₁₀H₁₆O; Mr = 152.0

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in mol, of H₂ that reacts with 1 mol of citral when all the C=C and C=O bonds are reduced using hydrogen and a nickel catalyst.
parts.answer: 3 mol

parts.label: d
parts.text: Only one of the two C=C bonds in citral can show cis/trans isomerism. Identify which and explain.
parts.answer: The C(CH₃)=CHCHO double bond; the (CH₃)₂C= carbon carries two identical CH₃ groups so that C=C cannot.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: For 2-methylbutan-1-ol, CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂OH, give (i) the molecular formula and (ii) the empirical formula.
parts.answer: (i) C₅H₁₂O (ii) C₅H₁₂O

parts.label: b
parts.text: In a skeletal formula, state what is represented by the end of a line and by each corner where lines meet.
parts.answer: A carbon atom (with enough hydrogen atoms to make four bonds).

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the empirical formula of hexane-1,6-diol, HO(CH₂)₆OH.
parts.answer: C₃H₇O

parts.label: a
parts.text: A skeletal formula shows a zig-zag chain of five carbon atoms with a double-bonded oxygen on the second carbon. Give the structural formula, molecular formula and name of the compound.
parts.answer: CH₃COCH₂CH₂CH₃; C₅H₁₀O; pentan-2-one

parts.label: b
parts.text: A skeletal formula shows a six-membered ring of carbon atoms, all single bonds, with an OH group at one corner. Give the molecular formula and name.
parts.answer: C₆H₁₂O; cyclohexanol

parts.label: a
parts.text: State three features of a homologous series.
parts.answer: Same general formula; same functional group / similar chemical properties; successive members differ by CH₂; gradual trend in physical properties.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give the general formula of (i) the alkenes (ii) the alcohols (iii) the carboxylic acids.
parts.answer: (i) CₙH₂ₙ (ii) CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH (iii) CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH (or CₙH₂ₙO₂)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the Mr of the alkane with nine carbon atoms. [Ar: C, 12.0; H, 1.0]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name three reagents that convert ethanoic acid into ethanoyl chloride.
parts.answer: phosphorus(V) chloride, PCl₅; phosphorus(III) chloride, PCl₃ (with heat); sulfur dichloride oxide (thionyl chloride), SOCl₂

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of ethanoic acid with SOCl₂.
parts.answer: CH₃COOH + SOCl₂ → CH₃COCl + SO₂ + HCl

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest why SOCl₂ is often preferred for this preparation.
parts.answer: The by-products SO₂ and HCl are gases and escape, so the acyl chloride is easy to separate.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the organic product of the reaction of ethanoyl chloride with each of: (i) water (ii) ethanol (iii) ammonia (iv) methylamine.
parts.answer: (i) ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH (ii) ethyl ethanoate, CH₃COOC₂H₅ (iii) ethanamide, CH₃CONH₂ (iv) N-methylethanamide, CH₃CONHCH₃

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write an equation for reaction (ii).
parts.answer: CH₃COCl + C₂H₅OH → CH₃COOC₂H₅ + HCl

parts.label: c
parts.text: State what is seen when ethanoyl chloride is added to water.
parts.answer: Steamy (white) fumes of HCl; vigorous reaction, heat given out.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the type of mechanism for the reaction between ethanoyl chloride and ammonia.
parts.answer: Nucleophilic addition–elimination

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe the mechanism in words, stating where each pair of electrons moves. (You may describe curly arrows in words.)
parts.answer:
1 The lone pair on the N of NH₃ attacks the δ+ carbonyl carbon.
2 At the same time the π electrons of C=O move onto the oxygen, giving a tetrahedral intermediate with O⁻ and N⁺.
3 The lone pair on O⁻ reforms the C=O and the C–Cl bond pair moves onto Cl, which leaves as Cl⁻.
4 Cl⁻ (or another NH₃) removes H⁺ from the N, giving CH₃CONH₂ and HCl (NH₄Cl).
parts.working:
M1 N lone pair attacks C of C=O
M1 C=O π pair to O / intermediate with O⁻ and N⁺
M1 C=O reforms and Cl⁻ leaves
M1 loss of H⁺ from N

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the carbonyl carbon of ethanoyl chloride is attacked much more readily than the carbon of chloroethane.
parts.answer: It is bonded to two electronegative atoms (O and Cl), making it strongly δ+, and it is planar/unhindered so the nucleophile can approach easily.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of phenol with benzoyl chloride, C₆H₅COCl.
parts.answer: C₆H₅OH + C₆H₅COCl → C₆H₅COOC₆H₅ + HCl

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why phenyl benzoate is made from benzoyl chloride and not by heating benzoic acid with phenol and an acid catalyst.
parts.answer: Phenol reacts only very slowly with carboxylic acids (its lone pair is delocalised into the ring, so it is a poor nucleophile); the acyl chloride is much more reactive.

parts.label: c
parts.text: 2.35 g of phenol is reacted with excess benzoyl chloride. The yield of phenyl benzoate is 78.0%. Calculate the mass of phenyl benzoate obtained. [Mr: phenol 94.0; phenyl benzoate 198.0]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the equation for the hydrolysis of ethanoyl chloride.
parts.answer: CH₃COCl + H₂O → CH₃COOH + HCl

parts.label: b
parts.text: 1.00 g of ethanoyl chloride is completely hydrolysed in water and the solution is titrated with 0.500 mol/dm³ NaOH. Calculate the volume of NaOH needed to neutralise all the acid formed. [Mr: CH₃COCl, 78.5]
parts.answer: 51.0 cm³
parts.working:
M1 n(CH₃COCl) = 1.00/78.5 = 0.0127 mol
M1 2 mol acid (CH₃COOH + HCl) per mol, so n(NaOH) = 0.0255 mol
A1 0.0255/0.500 = 0.0510 dm³ = 51.0 cm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest why the bottle of ethanoyl chloride must be kept tightly closed in a humid city such as Karachi.
parts.answer: It reacts with water vapour in the air, being hydrolysed to ethanoic acid and HCl.

stem: An acyl chloride RCOCl contains 38.4% chlorine by mass.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the Mr of the acyl chloride, and deduce the formula of R and the name of the compound. [Ar: C, 12.0; H, 1.0; O, 16.0; Cl, 35.5]
parts.answer: Mr = 92.4 (≈ 92.5); COCl = 63.5, so R = 29 = C₂H₅; propanoyl chloride, CH₃CH₂COCl
parts.working:
M1 35.5/0.384 = 92.4
M1 R = 92.4 − 63.5 ≈ 29 → C₂H₅
A1 propanoyl chloride

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give the structural formula and name of the product when this acyl chloride reacts with methylamine.
parts.answer: CH₃CH₂CONHCH₃, N-methylpropanamide

author: HomiLabs

stem: A few drops of each of ethanoyl chloride, chloroethane and chlorobenzene are added to separate test-tubes containing aqueous silver nitrate in ethanol at room temperature.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe what you would see in each tube.
parts.answer: Ethanoyl chloride: white precipitate immediately (with steamy fumes). Chloroethane: white precipitate forms slowly (on warming). Chlorobenzene: no precipitate.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain the difference in reactivity between chloroethane and chlorobenzene.
parts.answer: In chlorobenzene a lone pair on Cl overlaps with the delocalised π system of the ring, giving the C–Cl bond partial double-bond character so it is stronger and harder to break; the ring electrons also repel nucleophiles.
parts.working:
M1 Cl lone pair delocalised into ring
M2 C–Cl bond stronger / partial double bond

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Place ethanol, phenol, ethanoic acid and water in order of increasing acidity.
parts.answer: ethanol < water < phenol < ethanoic acid

parts.label: b
parts.text: State what is seen when sodium carbonate solution is added to (i) ethanoic acid and (ii) phenol.
parts.answer: (i) effervescence (CO₂ given off) (ii) no visible reaction / no effervescence

parts.label: c
parts.text: State which of the three organic compounds react with (i) sodium metal and (ii) aqueous sodium hydroxide.
parts.answer: (i) all three (ii) phenol and ethanoic acid only

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why phenol is a stronger acid than ethanol.
parts.answer: In the phenoxide ion the negative charge on O is delocalised into the benzene ring (a p orbital on O overlaps with the π system), which stabilises the anion. The ethoxide ion has no delocalisation.
parts.working:
M1 charge on phenoxide delocalised into ring
M2 anion stabilised, so dissociation more favourable; no delocalisation in ethoxide

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why ethanol is a weaker acid than water.
parts.answer: The ethyl group is electron-donating, which increases the negative charge density on O in the ethoxide ion, destabilising it.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why ethanoic acid is a stronger acid than phenol.
parts.answer: In the ethanoate ion the charge is delocalised over two electronegative oxygen atoms, which stabilises it more than delocalisation into a ring of carbon atoms.

stem: pKa values at 298 K: CH₃COOH 4.76; ClCH₂COOH 2.87; Cl₂CHCOOH 1.29; Cl₃CCOOH 0.65.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain the trend in pKa values.
parts.answer: Cl is electronegative and withdraws electron density (negative inductive effect) from the COO⁻ group, spreading the negative charge and stabilising the anion. More Cl atoms → greater stabilisation → more dissociation → stronger acid (lower pKa).
parts.working:
M1 Cl electron-withdrawing
M1 stabilises carboxylate anion / weakens O–H
M1 effect increases with number of Cl

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate Ka for chloroethanoic acid.
parts.answer: 1.35 × 10⁻³ mol/dm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: Predict, with a reason, whether 2-chloropropanoic acid or 3-chloropropanoic acid is the stronger acid.
parts.answer: 2-chloropropanoic acid: the Cl is closer to the COOH group, so its electron-withdrawing effect is greater.

author: HomiLabs

stem: Three unlabelled bottles contain aqueous ethanoic acid, an aqueous solution of phenol and ethanol.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe how you could identify each liquid using no more than two reagents. Give the observations for each liquid.
parts.answer: Add Na₂CO₃(aq) to each: only ethanoic acid effervesces (CO₂). Add bromine water to the other two: phenol decolourises the orange bromine water and gives a white precipitate; ethanol shows no change (stays orange). (Alternatively, neutral FeCl₃(aq) gives a violet colour with phenol and none with ethanol.)
parts.working:
M1 Na₂CO₃ (or NaHCO₃) test
A1 effervescence only with ethanoic acid
M1 bromine water (or neutral FeCl₃) to separate phenol from ethanol
A1 phenol: decolourised + white precipitate (or violet colour); ethanol: no change

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why phenol does not produce carbon dioxide from sodium carbonate solution.
parts.answer: Phenol is a weaker acid than carbonic acid (H₂CO₃ / HCO₃⁻), so it cannot protonate carbonate to release CO₂.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction of ethanoic acid with sodium carbonate.
parts.answer: 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the volume of CO₂, in cm³ at room conditions, produced when 0.600 g of ethanoic acid reacts with excess sodium carbonate. [Mr: CH₃COOH, 60.0; 1 mol gas = 24.0 dm³]
parts.answer: 120 cm³
parts.working:
M1 0.0100 mol acid → 0.00500 mol CO₂
A1 120 cm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: 0.940 g of phenol reacts with excess sodium. Write the equation and calculate the volume of hydrogen produced at room conditions. [Mr: phenol, 94.0]
parts.answer: 2C₆H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₆H₅ONa + H₂; 120 cm³
parts.working:
B1 equation
B1 0.0100 mol phenol → 0.00500 mol H₂ = 120 cm³

stem: pKa of phenol = 9.95 at 298 K.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the pH of a 0.0500 mol/dm³ solution of phenol at 298 K. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Suggest why 4-nitrophenol (pKa 7.15) is a much stronger acid than phenol (pKa 9.95).
parts.answer: The NO₂ group is strongly electron-withdrawing, so it draws the negative charge of the phenoxide ion further away from O (through the ring), increasing delocalisation and stabilising the anion.
parts.working:
M1 NO₂ electron-withdrawing
M2 anion further stabilised / charge more delocalised

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write equations for the reactions of phenol with (i) sodium hydroxide and (ii) sodium.
parts.answer: (i) C₆H₅OH + NaOH → C₆H₅ONa + H₂O (ii) 2C₆H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₆H₅ONa + H₂

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction of ethanol with sodium and name the organic product.
parts.answer: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂; sodium ethoxide

parts.label: a
parts.text:
What is the name of the ester formed from propanoic acid and methanol?
A propyl methanoate
B methyl propanoate
C methyl propanal
D propyl methyl ether
parts.answer: B methyl propanoate
parts.working: The alcohol part is named first (methyl) and the acid part becomes '-oate' (propanoate): CH₃CH₂COOCH₃. Propyl methanoate would be made from methanoic acid and propan-1-ol.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of ethanoic acid with propan-1-ol and name the ester formed.
parts.answer: CH₃COOH + CH₃CH₂CH₂OH ⇌ CH₃COOCH₂CH₂CH₃ + H₂O; propyl ethanoate

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the conditions needed for this reaction.
parts.answer: Concentrated sulfuric acid (catalyst); heat (warm/reflux)

parts.label: c
parts.text: State one use of esters.
parts.answer: Flavourings / perfumes / solvents (e.g. in nail-varnish remover)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the products of heating ethyl ethanoate under reflux with (i) dilute sulfuric acid and (ii) aqueous sodium hydroxide.
parts.answer: (i) ethanoic acid and ethanol (ii) sodium ethanoate and ethanol

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why hydrolysis with sodium hydroxide gives a higher yield than hydrolysis with dilute acid.
parts.answer: Acid hydrolysis is reversible and reaches equilibrium. With NaOH the acid formed is converted to the carboxylate ion, which does not react with the alcohol, so the reaction goes to completion.
parts.working:
M1 acid hydrolysis reversible / equilibrium
M2 carboxylate ion formed, so not reversible

parts.label: c
parts.text: State how ethanoic acid could be obtained from the products of reaction (ii).
parts.answer: Add excess strong acid (e.g. dilute HCl) to protonate the ethanoate ions, then distil.

stem:
A student heats 2.20 g of an ester under reflux with 50.0 cm³ of 1.00 mol/dm³ NaOH (an excess) for 30 minutes. After cooling, the excess NaOH is titrated with 1.00 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid using phenolphthalein indicator.
Titres (cm³): rough 25.40; 1st 25.05; 2nd 24.95; 3rd 25.00

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the mean titre, using only concordant results.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the amount of NaOH that reacted with the ester.
parts.working:
M1 NaOH added 0.0500 mol; excess = 0.02500 mol
A1 0.0500 − 0.0250 = 0.0250 mol

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the Mr of the ester and suggest the names of two esters it could be.
parts.answer: 88.0; e.g. ethyl ethanoate and methyl propanoate (or propyl methanoate)

parts.label: d
parts.text: Suggest why the mixture is heated under reflux rather than simply warmed in an open flask.
parts.answer: Hydrolysis is slow; reflux allows long heating without loss of the volatile ester / alcohol.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Methyl propanoate, CH₃CH₂COOCH₃, is heated under reflux with aqueous sodium hydroxide. What are the products?
A propanoic acid and methanol
B sodium propanoate and methanol
C sodium methanoate and propan-1-ol
D sodium ethanoate and ethanol
parts.answer: B sodium propanoate and methanol
parts.working: Alkaline hydrolysis breaks the ester into the alcohol (methanol) and the salt of the acid (sodium propanoate). A is the product of acid hydrolysis, not of NaOH.

stem: An ester with molecular formula C₅H₁₀O₂ is hydrolysed to give a carboxylic acid X and an alcohol Y. Oxidation of Y with acidified potassium dichromate(VI) gives propanone.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Identify the acid X, the alcohol Y and the ester. Give the structural formula of the ester.
parts.answer: X ethanoic acid; Y propan-2-ol; ester CH₃COOCH(CH₃)₂ (1-methylethyl ethanoate / propan-2-yl ethanoate)
parts.working:
B1 Y propan-2-ol (secondary alcohol giving a ketone)
B1 X ethanoic acid (C₅ − C₃ = C₂)
B1 ester formula

parts.label: b
parts.text: 6.00 g of X is heated with excess Y and a sulfuric acid catalyst. 6.12 g of the ester is obtained. Calculate the percentage yield. [Mr: X 60.0; ester 102.0]

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Propanoic acid is reduced with LiAlH₄ in dry ether. What is the organic product?
A propanal
B propan-1-ol
C propan-2-ol
D propane
parts.answer: B propan-1-ol
parts.working: LiAlH₄ reduces a carboxylic acid fully to a primary alcohol: CH₃CH₂COOH + 4[H] → CH₃CH₂CH₂OH + H₂O. Propanal is an intermediate that is reduced further.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the organic product when each compound is treated with NaBH₄: (i) butanal (ii) butanone (iii) butanoic acid.
parts.answer: (i) butan-1-ol (ii) butan-2-ol (iii) no reaction (NaBH₄ does not reduce carboxylic acids)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write an equation for the reduction of butanone, using [H] for the reducing agent.
parts.answer: CH₃COCH₂CH₃ + 2[H] → CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃

parts.label: c
parts.text: State why LiAlH₄ must be used in dry ether rather than in water.
parts.answer: LiAlH₄ reacts violently with water.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
3-oxobutanoic acid, CH₃COCH₂COOH, is treated with NaBH₄. What is the organic product?
A CH₃CH(OH)CH₂COOH
B CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₂OH
C CH₃COCH₂CH₂OH
D CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH
parts.answer: A CH₃CH(OH)CH₂COOH
parts.working: NaBH₄ reduces the ketone C=O to a secondary alcohol but does not reduce the COOH group. B is the product with LiAlH₄, which reduces both groups.

stem: Levulinic acid, CH₃COCH₂CH₂COOH, can be made from sugarcane waste (bagasse).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the structural formula of the product formed when levulinic acid reacts with NaBH₄.
parts.answer: CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₂COOH

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give the structural formula and name of the product formed with excess LiAlH₄, and write a balanced equation using [H].
parts.answer: CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₂CH₂OH, pentane-1,4-diol; CH₃COCH₂CH₂COOH + 6[H] → CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₂CH₂OH + H₂O
parts.working:
B1 structure
B1 name
B1 balanced equation (6[H], H₂O)

parts.label: c
parts.text: The product of (a) is chiral but the sample obtained does not rotate plane-polarised light. Explain why.
parts.answer: The carbonyl group is planar, so hydride (H⁻) attacks from either side with equal probability, giving a racemic mixture.
parts.working:
M1 planar C=O, attack from both sides equally
M2 racemic mixture, rotations cancel

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write an equation for the reduction of butanoic acid with LiAlH₄, using [H].
parts.answer: CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH + 4[H] → CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH + H₂O

parts.label: b
parts.text: 4.40 g of butanoic acid gives 2.96 g of butan-1-ol. Calculate the percentage yield. [Mr: butanoic acid 88.0; butan-1-ol 74.0]

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest a reagent that would convert butan-1-ol back into butanoic acid, and state the conditions.
parts.answer: Acidified potassium dichromate(VI), heat under reflux (excess oxidant)

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which substance does not react with aqueous ethanoic acid?
A magnesium
B copper
C calcium carbonate
D potassium hydroxide
parts.answer: B copper
parts.working: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it does not displace hydrogen from the weak acid. Magnesium gives H₂, calcium carbonate gives CO₂ and KOH is neutralised.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write equations for the reactions of ethanoic acid with (i) magnesium (ii) calcium carbonate (iii) sodium hydroxide.
parts.answer:
(i) 2CH₃COOH + Mg → (CH₃COO)₂Mg + H₂
(ii) 2CH₃COOH + CaCO₃ → (CH₃COO)₂Ca + H₂O + CO₂
(iii) CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why vinegar (dilute ethanoic acid) can be used to remove limescale (calcium carbonate) from a kettle.
parts.answer: Ethanoic acid reacts with CaCO₃ to form soluble calcium ethanoate, water and CO₂.

stem: 0.370 g of a monobasic carboxylic acid, CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH, is dissolved in water and titrated with 0.100 mol/dm³ NaOH. 50.0 cm³ of NaOH is needed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the amount of NaOH used.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the Mr of the acid and deduce its structural formula and name.
parts.answer: Mr = 74.0; CH₃CH₂COOH; propanoic acid
parts.working:
M1 n(acid) = 5.00 × 10⁻³ (1 : 1)
A1 Mr = 0.370/5.00 × 10⁻³ = 74.0
A1 CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH: 14n + 46 = 74, n = 2 → propanoic acid

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest a suitable indicator for this titration and explain your choice.
parts.answer: Phenolphthalein; weak acid–strong base titration has an equivalence point above pH 7.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the reagent and conditions used to oxidise ethanol to ethanoic acid.
parts.answer: Acidified potassium dichromate(VI) (K₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄), in excess; heat under reflux

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the colour change seen.
parts.answer: orange to green

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction, using [O] for the oxidising agent.
parts.answer: CH₃CH₂OH + 2[O] → CH₃COOH + H₂O

stem:
Propanoic acid can be made from bromoethane in two steps:
step 1: CH₃CH₂Br → intermediate
step 2: intermediate → CH₃CH₂COOH

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the reagent and conditions for step 1 and name the intermediate formed.
parts.answer: KCN in ethanol, heat under reflux; propanenitrile, CH₃CH₂CN

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give the reagent and conditions for step 2 and write the equation.
parts.answer: Dilute HCl (aq acid), heat under reflux; CH₃CH₂CN + 2H₂O + HCl → CH₃CH₂COOH + NH₄Cl

parts.label: c
parts.text: State one advantage of this route compared with the direct oxidation of an alcohol.
parts.answer: It increases the carbon chain by one carbon atom (makes propanoic acid from a C₂ compound).

author: HomiLabs

topic: Chemical energetics (A Level: lattice energy, Born–Haber, hydration)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Define the term lattice energy.
parts.answer: The enthalpy change when one mole of an ionic compound is formed from its gaseous ions under standard conditions.
parts.working:
M1 one mole of ionic compound/solid formed
M2 from gaseous ions (standard conditions)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write an equation, with state symbols, for the lattice energy of magnesium chloride.
parts.answer: Mg²⁺(g) + 2Cl⁻(g) → MgCl₂(s)

parts.label: c
parts.text: State whether lattice energy is exothermic or endothermic and explain why.
parts.answer: Exothermic: bonds (electrostatic attractions) form between oppositely charged ions, releasing energy.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Chemical energetics (A Level: lattice energy, Born–Haber, hydration)
stem: Data (kJ/mol): ΔHf⦵ NaCl(s) −411; ΔHat⦵ Na(s) +107; first ionisation energy of Na +496; ΔHat⦵ of chlorine (½Cl₂ → Cl) +122; first electron affinity of Cl −349.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the data to calculate the lattice energy of sodium chloride.
parts.answer: −787 kJ/mol
parts.working:
M1 LE = ΔHf − ΔHat(Na) − IE(Na) − ΔHat(Cl) − EA(Cl) = −411 − 107 − 496 − 122 + 349
A1 −787 kJ/mol

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the enthalpy change ½Cl₂(g) → Cl(g).
parts.answer: Standard enthalpy change of atomisation of chlorine

author: HomiLabs

topic: Chemical energetics (A Level: lattice energy, Born–Haber, hydration)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Define the standard enthalpy change of atomisation of an element.
parts.answer: The enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous atoms is formed from the element in its standard state under standard conditions.
parts.working:
M1 one mole of gaseous atoms formed
